result.headline: Throttle command dropped to 0 at t=110.797 s with no recorded cause; the aircraft then lost altitude and control tracking.
result.explanation: The control fault is the throttle command cut to 0 at 110.797 s, serving the throttle/motor loop (ch2). ch2 followed it, so the output stage is not at fault. Who or what commanded the cut is not in the recording.

evidence.quote: CONSTANT propulsion.throttle was varying, then held 0 from t=110.797 s to the end of the recording (11.495 s, 30 samples)
evidence.shows: The throttle command stopped varying and held 0 to the end, with no mode event beside it.

evidence.quote: CONSTANT actuator.output[ch[2]] was varying, then held 1100 from t=111.32 s to the end of the recording (11.184 s, 35 samples)
evidence.shows: The throttle-loop output went to 1100 us after the command cut. It follows the command (correlation 0.986 at lag 0.331 s), so it is not an independent freeze.

evidence.quote: CHANGE propulsion.throttle at t=110.797 s: 40 -> 0 % (step -40, 40x its usual variation)
evidence.shows: A sudden step to zero, not a gradual decay.

evidence.quote: ANOMALY a9 t=111.29 s: vehicle.attitude[pitch] followed control.attitude_setpoint[pitch] worse for good (typical |error| 1.042 -> 9.199) (see line 77; strength 3.448)
evidence.shows: Pitch tracking degraded right after the throttle cut, as expected without thrust.

evidence.quote: ANOMALY a11 t=112.321 s: vehicle.altitude[relative] changed level for good (49.974 -> 37.493 m)
evidence.shows: Altitude fell after the cut and reached 21.61 m by the end of the recording.

checked.check: Compared levels and tracking before and after t=16.42 s, the first anomaly.
checked.result: Velocity and yaw changed, but pitch tracking error stayed 1.09 -> 1.139 deg and roll 1.67 -> 1.913 deg. Large velocity swings repeat later, so this looks like a manoeuvre, not a fault.
